main_text.p: Fernelium. Sed ab utero ftrangulatus eft multiplex affectus. Conftat enim interperie frigida, diffolutione continui, & praua con formatione. In primis ipfum affectum effe frigidum fatis agnofcit Fernelius libro, de Cap.16. Partium morbis & Symptomatis. Deinde diffolutionem continui, & prauam ftructuram aperte declarant inflatio uteri, aut dilatatio. Totus nanq; uterus diftenditur inflaturie, ob cuius dilatationem, aut inflationem, non folum uentriculus & intefti na comprimuntur, fed etiam feptum tranfuerfum, quod quidem adeo interdu coarctatur, ut amplius dilatari nequeat. Propte rea hyfterice mulieres nonnunquam quafi femimortue iacent, quibus cotingit (quéadmodum inquit Galenus) fenfus ac motus priuatio, pulfus obfcurus & paruus, atque penitus interceptus. In aliquibus uero tum fenfus, tu motus adeft, ratioq; conftat, cæterum uix refpirant. Aliquibus etia uox intercipitur, quę tamen audiunt & uident. Loqui enim nequeunt penuria aeris, qui quidem uocis eft materia. Is namq; ob prohibitam diaphragmatis dilatationem efflari non poteft. Quibus fymptomatis omnibus ab utero ftrangulatum non effe to

page.notes: Catchword/continuation: the last line "omnibus ab utero ftrangulatum non effe to" is followed by a word "tius" beside the signature line; this is the start of the next page's catchword and is left out of the text. Marginal "Cap.16." is printed in the right margin and is transcribed as a note. Doubtful readings: "ratioq;" and "coarctatur" are read with reasonable confidence; "Fernelius" and "Galenus" are clear. The page has no visible reference mark in the text beside the marginal note, so no curly-brace marker is placed. Line "Fernelium." begins the page without indent and is treated as continuing from the previous page.
